title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a general, axiomatic version of the 'equation des lacets' (loop equation) material. That material is Grothendieck's own study of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group attached to the modular group. Here he takes an abstract group 𝔊 with two distinguished elements ρ, σ; the model case is 𝔊 = SL(2,Ẑ)' with ρ, σ 'modular', i.e. the torsion-type generators.

The objects carried over from the previous pages are:
- G_{ρ,σ}, a group of pairs (α,β).
- B_{ρ,σ} ⊂ G_{ρ,σ}.
- Z_ρ, Z_σ, the centralizers of ρ and σ in G_{ρ,σ}.
- A quotient homomorphism δ_G : G_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ}, together with its restrictions δ_B, δ_ρ, δ_σ.
- The bijection (34) B×Z_ρ×Z_σ ≅ G_{ρ,σ}, (u,a,b) ↦ (ua^{-1}, ub^{-1}).

On this page:

(36) He defines S_0Γ^0_{ρ,σ} = {(u,a,b) ∈ B×Z_ρ×Z_σ | δ(u) = δ_ρ(a) = δ_σ(b)}. This is the iterated fibre product B ×_Γ Z_ρ ×_Γ Z_σ.

(37) A marginal NB explains the prefix 'S'. It is modelled on the usage for 'simply connected' groups (cf. SL vs GL) and on SZ_ρ, SZ_σ, the kernels of the maps to Γ_{ρ,σ}.

(38) Restricting (34) gives a bijection of S_0Γ^0 onto the subset S_0𝒢_{ρ,σ} of pairs (ξ,η), with ξ = ua^{-1}, η = ub^{-1}.

Scholie. Transport of structure through (34) and (38) gives natural group structures on 𝒢_{ρ,σ} and S_0𝒢_{ρ,σ}. He asks to make the resulting group law explicit, and does so in (39):
- Each pair (ξ,η) = (αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1}, βσβ^{-1}σ^{-1}) determines an endomorphism u_{ξ,η} of 𝔊 with ρ ↦ ξρ = int(α)ρ and σ ↦ ησ = int(β)σ.
- The product is (α',β')(α,β) = (u'(α)α', u'(β)β').
- This is exactly the twisted ('crossed') composition law familiar from the Drinfeld/Ihara definition of GT, where (λ,f) acts by x ↦ x^λ, y ↦ f^{-1}y^λ f and composition twists f by the automorphism attached to the other factor. Here it is formulated for an arbitrary pair of elements ρ, σ.

(39)–(40) A subgroup L_0 embeds in SΓ^0 via ℓ ↦ (ℓ,1,1); the page text says 1 ↦ (1,1,1). This gives the exact sequence 1 → L_0 → SΓ^0 → τ_{ρ,σ} → 1, where (41) τ_{ρ,σ} := Z_ρ ×_Γ Z_σ.

A crossed-out passage defines M_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(𝔊) as the automorphisms that
- preserve the conjugacy classes of ρ and σ, and
- preserve the conjugacy class of L_0, i.e. f·u normalizes L_0 for some f.
This is a 'braid-like' or inertia-preserving automorphism group.

(42) There is an exact sequence 1 → SZ_ρ×SZ_σ → τ_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1.

The next page quotients by L_0 to obtain Γ^0_{ρ,σ}. It then checks that for 𝔊 = SL(2,Ẑ) with modular ρ, σ one recovers the objects of §48 IX.

Purpose: to abstract the structure of the GT-like group built in §48 into a general group-theoretic construction depending only on (𝔊, ρ, σ, L_0), with its natural extensions and group law.
errors: Equation numbering is inconsistent: (39) is used three times on this page (group law, the embedding of L_0, and the struck-out M_{ρ,σ}), and (40)–(42) are reused with different meanings on the next page.
The embedding of L_0 is written 'id ↦ (1,1,1)' here and corrected on the next page to ℓ ↦ (ℓ,1,1).

The letter u is used both for an element of B_{ρ,σ} and for the automorphism u_{ξ,η} of 𝔊, which blurs (38)/(39). Also, the sequence (42) as written on this page ends in Γ_{ρ,σ}, whereas the next page's analogue ends in γ_{ρ,σ}; the target quotient is not consistently named.
Surjectivity of τ_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} in (42) requires δ_ρ and δ_σ to be surjective. This holds by the next page's (45) but is not justified on this page.

ideas.what: Iterated fibre product B ×_Γ Z_ρ ×_Γ Z_σ as a 'simply connected' cover S_0Γ^0 of a GT-type group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (GT); this exact formulation unsure

ideas.what: Twisted group law on pairs (α,β) via the endomorphism u_{ξ,η}: ρ ↦ int(α)ρ, σ ↦ int(β)σ
ideas.modern_name: GT composition law (crossed product with self-action)

ideas.what: Group of automorphisms preserving the conjugacy classes of ρ, σ and of a subgroup L_0 (crossed out)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Teichmüller tower automorphisms in spirit only

ideas.what: Exact sequences 1 → L_0 → SΓ^0 → τ → 1 and 1 → SZ_ρ×SZ_σ → τ → Γ → 1
ideas.modern_name: group extensions from fibre products of centralizers

missed.claim: The page abstracts the GT-type group law to an arbitrary group with two distinguished elements and a subgroup L_0, building it from centralizers through iterated fibre products. Grothendieck's own route to GT-like groups via SL(2,Ẑ) ('variations sur l'équation des lacets') is undocumented in the literature beyond Drinfeld/Ihara. The content itself is routine group theory.
missed.quote: Expliciter cette structure de groupe ainsi trouvée notamment pour S𝒢_{ρ,σ}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents an independent, axiomatic approach to the GT composition law; it is of minor mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine but historically interesting technical steps in Grothendieck's private GT-type construction. The twisted group law is essentially the known GT composition law, and nothing on this page appears to be a missed result.
transcription_corrections: 'Γ^{ab}_{ρ,σ}' should be read Γ^0_{ρ,σ} (superscript '0' after a struck-out symbol), consistent with the next page.
'Sτ'_{ρ,σ}' should be SΓ^0_{ρ,σ} (= B ×_Γ Z_ρ ×_Γ Z_σ).
Margin top-left: roughly 'voir SΓ^0_{ρ,σ} dans §48, IX ff' (cross-reference), not 'Γ^ab'.
The fibre-product condition reads δ_B(u) = δ_ρ(a) = δ_σ(b).
In (39), 'ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}' is better read ξ = α ρ α^{-1} ρ^{-1}, i.e. the commutator α(ρ)ρ^{-1} as on the previous page; likewise for η.
